Missouri arrest record expungement guide
Before you proceed
Stop: the false-information ground always requires legal assistance before proceeding. Take this prepared packet and your own
account of what happened to a lawyer. LegalEase does not decide that the arrest was based on false information or that probable
cause is absent; the court must make those findings.

Arrange the three standard fingerprint cards described below first; they are required before filing, even though this packet can be
prepared now.

Your section 610.122 packet
Prepared for Jordan Lee Example for the civil division of the Circuit Court in Jackson County, Missouri. Review every prefilled fact
before filing. This packet concerns one arrest on 01/12/2023 by Kansas City Police Department.

CR145 is the petition. FI-05 is the confidential filing cover sheet, including all four official source pages and extra party pages as
needed. CR143 is included only because you indicated the receiving court requests a proposed order. No fee waiver was
requested. Keep these instructions separate from documents submitted to the court.

Confirm the selected basis and records
You selected the false-information branch: arrest based on false information; no probable cause now to believe you committed the
offense; no charges will be pursued; no related suspended imposition of sentence; and no related civil action pending. Review
each sworn statement in CR145.

Request the arrest or booking report and citation from the arresting agency. Obtain your fingerprint-based criminal-history record
from the Missouri State Highway Patrol to build and check the agency list; confirm its current search fees. If charges were filed on
the traffic ground, obtain certified dismissal, nolle-prosequi or acquittal records for every related charge from the court clerk.
Obtain any docket and accurate record-holder names and addresses. Verify the county where the arrest occurred, arrest date,
offense, citation, OCN if assigned, case number and court division. Stop and obtain legal assistance if your records contradict a
required statement; this packet does not decide eligibility.

Obtain three standard fingerprint cards before filing. Call a local police department or sheriff’s office to ask whether it takes
applicant fingerprint impressions for court expungement, can provide three cards in one visit, the current cost for each card,
whether cash is required, and what identification to bring. Start early. One card is filed with the court; one is sent by the clerk to
the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons; keep the third card. These cards differ from fingerprints for a
Highway Patrol criminal-history search, and you do not have to buy a criminal record merely to obtain them. The packet does not
fabricate the cards.

Review and execute
Compare every prefilled name, address, birth date, Social Security number, driver license, arrest fact, case and defendant
against your records. FI-05 is confidential: submit it using the court’s confidential filing procedure; do not attach an unredacted
copy to public instructions. The case-type table identifies XG for expungement of criminal/arrest records.

Do not sign CR145 beforehand. Take identification and sign its sworn statement before the notary, judge or clerk authorized to
administer the oath. Leave new case number, court ORI, court assignments, court findings, dates, file stamps, judicial and
notarial signatures to their owners. The address under the participant signature is prefilled; the signature remains blank.

The attached records checklist is part of these instructions: arrest/citation; criminal history; case and disposition documents if
charges were filed; complete record-holder/service addresses; fingerprint card; and financial records if requesting waiver.

File and provide notice
File CR145 with the clerk of the civil division of the circuit court for Jackson County, where the arrest occurred. Ask that clerk for
the current filing fee, payment method, required copies, filing method and local submission requirements. Do not substitute a
conviction-expungement form for this arrest route.

Before you proceed
Stop: the false-information ground always requires legal assistance before proceeding. Take this prepared packet and your own

Your section 610.122 packet
Prepared for Jordan Lee Example for the civil division of the Circuit Court in Jackson County, Missouri. Review every prefilled fact
before filing. This packet concerns one arrest on 01/12/2023 by Kansas City Police Department.

CR145 is the petition. FI-05 is the confidential filing cover sheet, including all four official source pages and extra party pages as
needed. No proposed order was requested. No fee waiver was requested. Keep these instructions separate from documents
submitted to the court.

Confirm the selected basis and records
You selected the false-information branch: arrest based on false information; no probable cause now to believe you committed the
offense; no charges will be pursued; no related suspended imposition of sentence; and no related civil action pending. Review
each sworn statement in CR145.

Request the arrest or booking report and citation from the arresting agency. Obtain your fingerprint-based criminal-history record
from the Missouri State Highway Patrol to build and check the agency list; confirm its current search fees. If charges were filed on
the traffic ground, obtain certified dismissal, nolle-prosequi or acquittal records for every related charge from the court clerk.
Obtain any docket and accurate record-holder names and addresses. Verify the county where the arrest occurred, arrest date,
offense, citation, OCN if assigned, case number and court division. Stop and obtain legal assistance if your records contradict a
required statement; this packet does not decide eligibility.

contract.legalName: Verified Petition for Expungement of Arrest Records (Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124)
contract.publicName: An arrest based on false information
contract.mechanism: Sections 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124 were read in full from the Revisor's current text and together they are the strongest record-clearing remedy Missouri has. § 610.122, effective 28 August 2021, allows any record of arrest recorded under § 43.503 to be expunged on either of two alternative grounds. The first is that the court determines the arrest was based on false information and that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge to believe the individual committed the offense, no charges will be pursued as a result of the arrest, and the subject did not receive a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or any related offense. The second is that the court determines the person was arrested for, or subsequently charged with, a misdemeanor offense of chapter 303 or any moving violation as defined in § 302.010 other than an intoxication-related traffic offense as defined in § 577.023, that each offense or violation related to the arrest was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, and that the person is not a commercial driver's licence holder and was not operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest. § 610.122.2 adds that a record is eligible only if no civil action is pending relating to the arrest or the records sought to be expunged. § 610.123 supplies the procedure and it is unusually specific: a verified petition filed in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, which shall be dismissed if it does not contain the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, Social Security number and address at the time of arrest, the offense charged, the date of arrest, the county and any municipality of arrest, the arresting agency, the case number and court, and the petitioner's fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card at the time of filing, forwarded to the central repository for the sole purpose of positively identifying the petitioner. The petition names as defendants all law enforcement agencies, courts, prosecuting attorneys, central state depositories and others the petitioner has reason to believe may possess the records, and the court's order does not affect any person or entity not named. The court sets a hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing and gives reasonable notice to each named entity. § 610.123.4 makes relief mandatory on the findings — if the court finds the petitioner is entitled to expungement of any record that is the subject of the petition, it shall enter an order directing expungement — which closes an open question the review could not answer. § 610.124 then requires that all records ordered expunged be destroyed, or blacked out where destruction is not feasible because of the permanent nature of the record books, removed from all electronic files maintained with the State of Missouri, and that the central repository request the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge the records from its files. § 610.124.2 gives any petitioner, or agency protesting the expungement, the ordinary civil right of appeal. This is the one Missouri track where the word destroyed is accurate.
exclusions: Any arrest where the subject received a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or for any offense related to the arrest (§ 610.122.1(1)(c)). This bars the false-information ground outright.

Any record where a civil action is pending relating to the arrest or to the records sought to be expunged (§ 610.122.2). This is a bar on both grounds and it reaches civil actions the participant may not think of as related.

On the moving-violation ground, any intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense as defined under § 577.001. Those are excluded expressly and belong on the § 610.130 route if anywhere.
On the moving-violation ground, any person who is a commercial driver's licence holder or who was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest (§ 610.122.1(2)(b)).
On the moving-violation ground, any offense or violation related to the arrest that was not nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted. Every related offense must have ended that way.
An offense that is neither a chapter 303 misdemeanor nor a moving violation as defined in § 302.010, where the participant is relying on the moving-violation ground rather than on false information.
An arrest that resulted in a conviction, which is not reachable under § 610.122 on either ground and runs on § 610.140 instead.

waitingPeriods.duration: none. Neither § 610.122 nor § 610.123 states a waiting period, and none is implied. What the false-information ground requires instead is a present-tense finding — that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge — so the question is the state of the evidence now rather than the passage of time.

Where the arrest occurred in a municipality the municipality is named in the petition but the filing is still in the circuit court's civil division for that county.

If you are relying on the moving-violation ground: was every offense or violation connected to that arrest nolle prossed, dismissed, or did you get a not-guilty finding on each? If even one is outstanding or resulted in a conviction, this ground does not apply.
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the participant selects the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground.

generationRequirements.question: Was the offense a drink- or drug-driving offense, or an intoxication-related boating offense? Those are excluded from this route.
At the time of the arrest, did you hold a commercial driver licence, or were you driving a commercial motor vehicle? Answer for the time of the arrest, not for now.

Is any civil lawsuit pending that relates to this arrest or to the records you want expunged — for example a claim against the police, a wrongful-arrest suit, an insurance dispute or an employment claim arising from the arrest? Any pending civil action bars this route.
Have you been convicted of any misdemeanor or felony, before or after this arrest?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this arrest? Include the arresting agency, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Highway Patrol troop, the Missouri Criminal Records Repository, the prosecutor's office for the county or municipality, and the court divisions involved.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
Have you arranged to get three standard fingerprint cards from a local law enforcement agency? You need them before you file.
Have you arranged to sign the petition in front of a notary, a judge or a clerk? It must be sworn before one of the three.
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

participantFilingRequirements.name: Three standard fingerprint cards
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A local law enforcement agency — a municipal police department or county sheriff's department that takes applicant prints
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Arrest report or booking record
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Make an open-records request to the arresting agency for the arrest or booking record. It supplies the date of arrest, the citation number, the offense charged and the agency name, all of which § 610.123 makes mandatory contents of the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified record of the dismissal, nolle prosequi or not-guilty finding
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the charge was filed
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed and the participant is relying on the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the entry disposing of each offense related to the arrest. The ground requires that every related offense or violation was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, so the participant needs the disposition for each one, not just the lead charge.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is how the participant builds the agency list and confirms the prior-and-subsequent-conviction condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant is relying on the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground, or where commercial driver licence status is in any doubt.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record. It shows the offense classification and whether a commercial driver licence was ever issued, and commercial licence status at the time of arrest is an outright bar on the moving-violation ground.

manualCompletionItems.item: The selection between the two sworn grounds
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR145 page 1, the two checkbox paragraphs
manualCompletionItems.why: The review is right that the choice between the two grounds is the whole eligibility determination. LegalEase asks the factual questions and shows the participant which ground their answers point to, but the selection is sworn and is theirs.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that the arrest was based on false information
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR145 page 1, first ground — recited only from the participant's own words
manualCompletionItems.why: The review lists this third among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track. It is a factual showing about someone else's conduct and it is the participant's to make.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that there is no probable cause to believe the petitioner committed the offense
manualCompletionItems.why: Fourth on the same list. It is a present-tense legal conclusion about the state of the evidence, which is exactly what § 610.122.1(1)(a) makes the court determine.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any assertion that the participant is not a commercial driver licence holder
manualCompletionItems.why: Fifth on the same list: never assert commercial licence status without confirming it. The participant answers, and the driver record confirms their answer.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number and the Court ORI number
manualCompletionItems.why: Both are assigned by the clerk at filing.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets the hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing and supplies the details afterwards.

packetInstructions: This is the one Missouri track where destroyed is accurate. § 610.124 requires records ordered expunged to be destroyed, or blacked out where destruction is not feasible because of the permanent nature of the record books, removed from all Missouri electronic files, with the central repository requesting the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge its files. Destruction language must never migrate to a § 610.140 closure.

Filing is in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest — a different court and a different division from the § 610.140 routes. The packet says so plainly, because a participant who files this on the criminal side will be sent away.

The full Social Security number goes on the face of CR145, not only on the confidential cover sheet, because § 610.123.1(1)(f) makes it a mandatory content of the petition and directs dismissal where the information is not given. This is the single exception to Missouri's ordinary rule of confining the number to FI-05, and it exists because the controlling statute and the controlling form both require it.

The clerk's printed distribution steps are reproduced in the participant packet so the participant can check they happened: a copy of the petition to the prosecuting attorney, a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository, and notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney and to each entity named.
The order does not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant (§ 610.123.2). The same agency-completeness warning as the § 610.140 routes applies, and the participant verifies the list.

The standard fingerprint card is required before filing and is a mandatory content of the petition under § 610.123.1(7). It is obtained from a local law enforcement agency, three cards are wanted, and it never delays generation of the packet. It is sequenced at the front of the participant's task list.
participantQuestions: Whether any civil action is pending relating to the arrest or the records is asked early and broadly, because § 610.122.2 makes it an outright bar and participants do not think of an insurance dispute or an employment claim as related.
scopeRestrictions: Commercial driver licence holders and anyone operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of arrest are outside the moving-violation ground, and intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses are outside it entirely.
